ambiguities.description: Optional enrollment and grade timing: The transcript states 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in' (line 31), implying that grades are only assigned to enrolled students. However, it is unclear (1) whether enrollment in an offering is mandatory or optional for students, and (2) whether a grade is mandatory for every enrollment, or only assigned at the end of the semester. The model currently assumes enrollment is optional but grades are mandatory given enrollment. If some students can audit or drop courses, the enrollment-to-grade relationship may be more complex.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings... At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Instructor capacity constraint: The transcript states 'An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester' (line 11), which confirms an instructor can teach multiple offerings. However, it does not specify if there is an upper limit on how many offerings one instructor can teach, or any workload constraints. The model currently allows unbounded multiplicity.

source_references.excerpt: An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Offering capacity enforcement: The transcript mentions that each offering has a 'maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll' (line 23), but does not state whether the system enforces this cap or merely tracks it. The model includes MaxCapacity as an attribute but does not formally constrain the number of enrolled students.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll.

ambiguities.description: Semester date relationship: The transcript states a semester 'has a start date and an end date' (line 27), but does not explicitly state that the end date must be after the start date, or define the relationship between these dates (e.g., inclusive/exclusive boundaries). The model treats them as independent date attributes.

source_references.excerpt: A semester has a start date and an end date.
